example.status: Illustrative process, not a patient outcome
example.question: “My child wants to come outside with us. How can putting on shoes become something they take part in?”
steps: Start with what your child can do.
Describe how your child chooses shoes, sits, reaches or asks for help. The starting picture includes the support that makes the moment possible.
Agree a meaningful part of getting ready. Communication, movement, sensory comfort or sequencing support follows that individual goal.
Make the idea work at home.
Ask for a manageable opportunity during a real outing routine, with clear guidance on what to offer and what to notice.
Bring back what happened. Discuss what your child took part in, what help still mattered and which next step would be useful.

stages.title: Understand abilities
stages.text: Start with strengths, everyday observations and suitable assessment. Read AbilityScore with the child’s age, context and skills.

stages.title: Plan for readiness
stages.text: Discuss what you want to make possible and agree useful priorities. Readiness views support professional judgement.

stages.title: Choose relevant support
stages.text: Bring in the therapies, educational support or health review that fit this child. Every child does not need every service.

stages.title: Practise in everyday life
stages.text: Use manageable, guided practice in meaningful routines. Family participation connects the work with daily life.

stages.title: Track and correct
stages.text: Bring relevant observations back into review. Ask what became useful, what support remains and what needs to change.

stages.title: Reassess and repeat
stages.text: Compare abilities and context over time. Continue, adapt or complete support according to the child’s needs.

stages.title: Grow independence and participation
stages.text: Keep self-sufficiency, learning, relationships and mainstream participation in view. Progress is individual.

questions.answer: Yes, use the national team to discuss your child’s priorities and ask which assessment, support and professional can be arranged at Nandyala. questions.question: What will a first conversation help me understand?
questions.answer: You can describe a meaningful everyday moment, discuss present abilities and ask about an appropriate assessment or support. Confirm who will meet your child, what the visit includes, how the family participates and how progress would be reviewed before deciding.
